definitions.gloss: sense of camaraderie; solidarity; fellow feeling; group consciousness
definitions.explanation: The feeling of belonging to a group and identifying with its members. Can be positive (team spirit) or negative (exclusionary in-group mentality).

examples.japanese: {仲間|なかま}{意識|いしき}が{強|つよ}いチームだ。
examples.english: It's a team with a strong sense of camaraderie.

examples.japanese: {合宿|がっしゅく}を{通|とお}じて{仲間|なかま}{意識|いしき}が{高|たか}まった。
examples.english: Our sense of solidarity deepened through the training camp.

examples.japanese: {仲間|なかま}{意識|いしき}が{強|つよ}すぎると、{外部|がいぶ}の{人|ひと}を{受|う}け{入|い}れにくくなることがある。
examples.english: If the group consciousness is too strong, it can become difficult to accept outsiders.

notes:
A compound of {仲間|なかま} (companion, fellow member) and {意識|いしき} (consciousness, awareness). Describes the psychological bond within a group. While often used positively to describe team spirit, it can also refer to exclusionary cliquishness when carried too far.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仲間|なかま}{意識|いしき}が{強|つよ}い: to have a strong sense of camaraderie
- {仲間|なかま}{意識|いしき}を{高|たか}める: to strengthen group solidarity
- {仲間|なかま}{意識|いしき}が{生|う}まれる: a sense of camaraderie develops
- {仲間|なかま}{意識|いしき}を{持|も}つ: to have a sense of belonging

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {連帯感|れんたいかん}: sense of solidarity — more formal, emphasizes mutual support and unity
- {帰属意識|きぞくいしき}: sense of belonging — focuses on identifying with an organization or community
- {一体感|いったいかん}: sense of unity — feeling of being one with a group, often in collective experiences
